title: Parents take children out of big schools

paragraphs: More Danish parents are pulling their children out of mainstream schools. They argue that the traditional education system is far too rigid for neurodivergent kids.

Children with autism or attention disorders, like 12-year-old Olav, often struggle with noisy classrooms and fixed daily schedules. Because public schools lack resources and specialized programs, many families have turned to alternative support systems, such as parent-led clubs. These spaces allow children to learn at their own pace through practical activities, like organic farming, while giving them a safe environment free from pressure.

While politicians worry about falling academic standards in reading and math, educational researchers argue that the school system itself needs urgent reform rather than forcing children to fit into outdated models. These alternative clubs aim to rebuild confidence and help kids rebuild their relationship with learning.

paragraphs: In Denmark, more and more parents are keeping their children home from traditional schools. Many neurodivergent children, like 12-year-old Olav, who has autism, find normal classrooms too loud and stressful.

Because schools lack special resources, parents are creating alternative clubs. In these clubs, kids can learn outside by doing practical things, like working on organic farms or building boats, without feeling stressed.

While government officials worry about test scores in reading and math, experts say the school system is old and needs big changes. Parents hope these new groups will give their kids a safe space to grow, feel happy again, and slowly return to learning.

paragraphs: Many parents in Denmark are taking their kids out of big schools. Normal classrooms are too loud and hard for some children.

A boy named Olav has autism. He only goes to school a few hours a week. He mostly learns outside on a farm with his family. Parents are starting local groups where kids can play, work with their hands, and feel safe without stress.
Experts say that schools need to change because kids learn in different ways today. These groups help families stay happy and keep learning every day.
